text:
Maria Chen: Quick sync — we need to finalize rollout plan for the regional throttling feature (affects routing + batching). Decision points: staged percentages, region-specific thresholds, blackout windows, and fallback behavior. I think shadow -> 2% -> 20% with auto-fallback when latency exceeds thresholds. Opinions?

Alex Rivera: +1 to shadow first. Strong preference to evaluate on p95 not p99 for initial gating. p99 tends to be noisy for small canaries.

Samir Patel: Agree on p95 but with region baselines — APAC p95 is typically ~180ms higher on our infra, so absolute thresholds should be regionalized.

Jess O'Neill: How long are we planning blackout windows during rollout? Need to avoid major business hours for important customers. Weekend vs weekday policy?

Paul Li: Proposal: daily maintenance blackout 02:00-04:00 UTC for heavy changes + a separate emergency 30m global kill window. For staged rollouts, do canaries outside peak hours per region.

Maria Chen: Good. Also need a clear decay policy for flags: if a feature flag receives <100 requests in 24h during a rollout stage, auto-decrease to previous stage and alert on-call.

Alex Rivera: We should codify metric pass/fail for A/B slices. Suggested success criteria: 1) success_rate delta >= -2% (relative), 2) cost_per_1k_tokens delta <= +10%, 3) p95 latency delta <= +200ms and absolute p95 < 1500ms. If any fail, immediate rollback for that slice.

Samir Patel: +1. Add an objective for error-rate (5xx) not to rise >0.2 percentage points. Also check cold-start time for new hosts during the canary.

Jess O'Neill: For A/B tests we also need sample size minimums so metrics are stable. Recommend minimum 10k impressions per slice before promoting.

Maria Chen: Sounds good. For fallback: prefer automatic fallback to baseline model variant + route-level throttling when p95 > threshold for 5m. Manual rollback if rollback_count > 2 within 1h.

Paul Li: Can we express the policy as a small config? i.e.

```
{
  "stages": ["shadow","2%","20%"],
  "metrics": {"p95_ms": 1500, "max_p95_delta_ms": 200, "min_impressions": 10000},
  "fallback": {"action": "route_to_baseline", "window_minutes": 5},
  "decay": {"requests_threshold_24h": 100}
}
```

Samir Patel: That looks good as a starting point. One tweak: make the p95_ms value region-overrides map instead of single value.

Alex Rivera: Also include a kill-switch tag in the flag metadata so Sales/Support can temporarily opt customers out by adding tenant IDs to an exclusion list.

Maria Chen: Noted. Ops question: how long do we hold a canary before moving to next stage? My gut: 60m stable window + 15m observation post-promotion. Thoughts?

Jess O'Neill: 60m seems fine for latency metrics but for A/B success rate and cost you might need longer. Maybe 4h for the 20% stage before GA unless metrics are extremely stable.

Paul Li: Agreed — 60m for small stages, 4h for larger. Add automatic rollback TTL: if we rollback after promotion, do not re-promote the same slice for 24h without a manual review.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary run: 2026-03-24T02:30:00Z (shadow + 2% warmup) — toggle:regional-throttle-v1, owner:@maria.chen

Maria Chen: Thanks — I'll update the rollout doc and the feature flag config in the console. Next steps: Alex to draft per-region threshold table, Samir to add region baseline numbers, Jess to outline blackout schedule matrix, Paul to add kill-switch + rollback TTL to runbook.

Alex Rivera: I'll drop a spreadsheet with thresholds by EOD.

Samir Patel: Adding baseline numbers now, will share in thread.

Jess O'Neill: I'll coordinate with Support for customer blackout exceptions.

Paul Li: I'll update runbook and add automated alerts to PagerDuty for threshold breaches.

Maria Chen: Great — aim to land this in staging next week. Tagging @deploy-bot for the scheduled smoke canary. :thumbsup:
